subject: Immediate: elevated 5xx/429 — capacity oversubscribe causing retry storms
messages:
From: Alex Dunn <ops@fintechnow.com>
To: support@redwood.ai
Cc: infra@fintechnow.com
Date: Fri, 15 May 2027 21:12:00 -0400
Subject: Urgent — sudden 5xx/429 spikes during batch window (FinTech Now)

Hi team,

We started a nightly reconciliation job at ~20:50 ET and within 15 minutes we saw a rapid increase in 429s and then a cascade of 5xx responses across our production requests. Latency ballooned (p95 from ~120ms to 4s) and several timeouts occurred. Our customers experienced failed payouts.

Attached: perf_dump_20270515.log (sampling), and a screenshot of the autoscaler dashboard showing node utilization.

We haven't changed our request patterns — the same batch runs every night. This is critical; we need an immediate mitigation and an ETA for a fix. Can you move us off saturated hosts or scale us up?

Please escalate — this impacts revenue.

Thanks,
Alex Dunn
Head of Ops, FinTech Now
[Attachment: perf_dump_20270515.log (text)]
[Attachment: autoscale-dashboard.png (image)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 15 May 2027 21:25:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Urgent — sudden 5xx/429 spikes during batch window (FinTech Now)

Alex — thank you for the heads up and the perf dump. We're treating this as priority P1 and I've looped in engineering and ops.

Immediate actions we're initiating now (ETA within 15–30m):
- Shift routing for FinTech Now to warm fallback capacity in a different pool to drain pressure on the saturated hosts.
- Temporarily increase the Dedicated pool max by +2x burst nodes for the next 2 hours to absorb the batch load.
- Disable scale-down for 20m to prevent oscillation while traffic stabilizes.

Aditya/Markus — please confirm you see the perf dump and autoscale screenshot and confirm the routing change. Monica, I'll send a customer update draft shortly.

Alex — we'll confirm when the routing change completes and provide an ETA for root cause.

-Lauren
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 15 May 2027 21:36:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Urgent — sudden 5xx/429 spikes during batch window (FinTech Now)

Lauren — I pulled the perf_dump and the cluster snapshot. Quick summary of what I'm seeing: 
- Dedicated pool for FinTech Now hit >98% GPU utilization across the primary node set within ~10 minutes of the batch window start.
- Autoscaler reacted but with a ~45s average decision latency; new nodes came online too late to prevent KV-cache thrash.
- Once the KV cache started evicting, cold starts amplified per-request latency and client-side retry logic turned a bounded spike into a retry storm, generating additional load and subsequent 5xx responses.

Root causes (hypothesis):
1) Oversubscription of the pool relative to the peak seq_len-heavy workload for that batch job. Our scale-up thresholds are tuned for steady-growth traffic and miss the short, high-signal batch.
2) Scale-up path has constrained warm-up: kernel selection and model weights memory residency took multiple seconds on new nodes — we need faster warm paths or pre-warmed standby nodes for scheduled heavy jobs.

Mitigations applied (already in progress):
- Route FinTech Now traffic to the warmed fallback pool (lauren noted this).
- Forced allocation of 4 burst nodes (we may need 6 if load doesn't fall).
- Reduced the autoscaler evaluation window to 10s for this pool and bumped the scale-up aggressiveness.

Longer-term fixes to propose to the product/ops roadmap:
- Standby pre-warmed burst instances for large scheduled jobs (configurable per-customer).
- Faster model residency via checkpointed memory images for common customers.
- Add a fast-path for lowering client retry windows on detected autoscale events (circuit-breaker at edge).

Logs attached: cluster_snapshot_20270515.json — I'll follow with a trimmed log bundle.

-Aditya
Sr. Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
[Attachment: perf_dump_20270515.log (text, trimmed)]

Subject: Re: Urgent — sudden 5xx/429 spikes during batch window (FinTech Now)

Alex — really sorry for the disruption. We have routing changes live and are watching metrics. We'll keep you updated every 15 minutes while this is active.

Customer-facing summary (what we'll communicate):
- What happened: a scheduled batch triggered a short, high-memory workload that oversubscribed the Dedicated pool and exposed an autoscaler warm-up gap. That led to cache evictions, request retries, and cascading 5xx responses.
- Immediate fix: traffic routed to backup capacity and burst nodes allocated; retries should subside as load stabilizes.
- Next steps: post-mortem within 72 hours, follow-up action items, and a proposal for scheduled pre-warming or a burst SLA for your largest nightly jobs.

Would you like us to proactively schedule a short maintenance window this weekend to run a controlled test? We can also offer a service credit for the disruption — happy to discuss the right level.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 16 May 2027 00:12:00 -0400
Subject: Exec note: incident impact & recommended credits

Team — quick exec summary for Lauren and GTM stakeholders: 
- Impact: FinTech Now saw ~11% failed requests for a 22-minute window (20:52–21:14 ET). We observed elevated 5xx/429 across ~3 customer-facing clusters due to retry amplification. Revenue-sensitive endpoints affected: payouts and reconciliation.
- Scope: primary impact limited to FinTech Now and two small customers sharing the Dedicated node farm; no region-wide outage.
- Financial/contract considerations: FinTech Now is on an annual committed Dedicated plan (medium-tier). They will expect remediation and likely a credit.

Recommendation: authorize a goodwill credit of 10% of last month's committed spend or a $25k credit (whichever is smaller) pending the post-mortem outcome. Also recommend offering a free week of pre-warmed burst capacity for their nightly jobs while we implement a permanent fix.

I'll prepare a short exec slide for GTM and finance; Lauren, please confirm if you'd like me to route the approval now.

-Markus
VP, Platform Operations
